# review-report — checklist

Two modes. **Create**: run it over a report before sending it. **Audit**: evaluate a report
someone else wrote — including one an agent wrote — and say what to change.

Priorities: **P0** the report cannot be acted on · **P1** expected on anything a human will
read · **P2** polish.

Every criterion traces to an entry in `field-notes.md`. Where a check is mechanical, it says so
instead of repeating the rule.

## Contents

- [Shape — can this report be aggregated and acted on?](#shape--can-this-report-be-aggregated-and-acted-on)
- [Findings — is each one actionable on its own?](#findings--is-each-one-actionable-on-its-own)
- [Scope — does the report stay inside the change?](#scope--does-the-report-stay-inside-the-change)

## Report format

```md
## <report under audit>
Score: P0 ✗ 0 · P1 ✗ 0 · P2 ✗ 0

| Prio | Section | Problem | Proposed fix |
| :- | :- | :- | :- |

Deliberately skipped: <item> — <reason>
```

---

## Shape — can this report be aggregated and acted on?

A report is read once and acted on by someone who was not there. Everything here exists so two
reports about the same change can be merged without being rewritten.

- [ ] **P0** The first line is `Verdict: block | approve with comments | clean`, one of those
      three words exactly. Anything else cannot gate a merge.
- [ ] **P0** The verdict follows the findings: `block` if any finding is blocking, `approve with
      comments` if there is anything at all, `clean` if there is nothing.
- [ ] **P0** Severity uses the four levels of `craft:reviewer-contract` — blocking, defect, risk,
      note — and no others. An invented scale aggregates with nothing.
- [ ] **P0** No style findings. Anything a linter, formatter or type checker decides is a missing
      rule, routed to `craft:rule-to-lint`, not a line in the report.
- [ ] **P1** `Not verified` is present and names the tool that was not run, with the findings
      that depend on it. "I read it" and "I ran it" are different claims.
- [ ] **P1** Questions to the author are their own section, each with the assumption made
      meanwhile. A question inside a finding is answered by nobody.
- [ ] **P1** `risk` and `note` are capped at three each, highest first, with one line saying how
      many were dropped.
- [ ] **P1** At least one `note` where a correct-looking-wrong pattern exists, saying why it is
      right. This is the level reviewers skip, and the one that prevents a future regression.
- [ ] **P2** The report would still be legible if the diff were not open next to it.

### Anti-patterns

- A verdict phrased as an opinion ("looks good to me, two things though").
- Findings grouped by file instead of by severity, so the reader has to rank them.
- A summary paragraph above the verdict. The verdict is the summary.

---

## Findings — is each one actionable on its own?

A finding is a unit of work for someone else. It is finished when that person can act without
asking a question.

- [ ] **P0** Every finding carries `path:line`. A finding with no location is skipped.
- [ ] **P0** Every finding states the consequence, not only the observation. "`catch {}` swallows
      the audit failure, so a cancelled order has no audit record" is a finding; "empty catch
      block" is a lint rule.
- [ ] **P0** The level matches the definition in `craft:reviewer-contract`, not the reviewer's
      sense of how annoying it is.
- [ ] **P1** A suggested fix is the smallest change that resolves the finding. Past a short
      snippet it is a design, and a design belongs in a question.
- [ ] **P1** No finding asserts behaviour the reviewer did not verify without saying so. A guess
      presented as a fact costs the whole report its credibility once found.
- [ ] **P1** Two findings with the same cause are one finding, with both locations.
- [ ] **P2** A finding that is cheap to fix and a finding that is expensive to fix say which.

### Anti-patterns

- A finding that is a question in disguise ("is this intentional?") placed in the findings table.
- Repeating the same finding once per occurrence, which inflates the count and buries the rest.
- A fix suggestion that rewrites code the finding does not concern.

---

## Scope — does the report stay inside the change?

- [ ] **P0** Nothing true before the change appears in the findings or affects the verdict. It
      goes under `Out of scope`, or it goes nowhere.
- [ ] **P0** Code outside the diff was read where it was needed to judge the change, and the
      report says so when a finding depends on it. Read widely, report narrowly.
- [ ] **P1** `Out of scope` findings are one line each, with a location, and no severity — they
      are a handover, not a judgement on this change.
- [ ] **P1** When `blocking` plus `defect` passes ten, the report says the change needs splitting
      instead of listing all of them.
- [ ] **P1** Missing tooling (no test setup, no linter) is reported as a condition under `Not
      verified`, not as a defect in the change — unless the change was supposed to add it.
- [ ] **P2** Where the change is right in a way a future reader might undo, that is a `note`.

### Anti-patterns

- A review of the file instead of the change. The author will read the whole report as unfair,
  and will be right.
- Pre-existing debt promoted to a blocking finding because it is adjacent to the diff.
- An `Out of scope` section used to review the rest of the repository.
